criterion: Acceptance: 2 parallel appends never get the same id; takeover by atomic mv
finding: Possible double takeover of one stale lock: age check and mv are not one step, so a late waiter can move a fresh lock.
why: The SDD landmine says '2 waiters can take over one stale lock'; waiter C that read the old age can mv the new holder B's fresh lock, and B's holds_lock check leaves a gap before the append, so B and C can mint the same id.
fix: Re-check the lock's age/owner after the mv (put a fresh lock back or abort the mint), or make the takeover compare the owner token it saw.
evidence:
age=$(lock_age "$lock_dir") || return 1; [ "$age" -ge 10 ] || return 1; mv "$lock_dir" "$grave" ... (then) holds_lock && break ... printf '%s
' "${line/...}" >> ledger

criterion: Acceptance: gate walks skip an entry that vanishes mid-walk
finding: The walk fix re-runs the whole walk up to 5 times and then raises, instead of skipping the vanished entry.
why: Acceptance says the walks 'skip an entry that vanishes mid-walk'; under repeated lock churn the 5th failure still exits the gate with a traceback.
fix: Walk with os.walk/scandir that ignores FileNotFoundError per folder, or record the retry cap as a decision in plan/DECISIONS.md.
evidence: tries = 5 ... except FileNotFoundError: tries -= 1; if not tries: raise

finding: Lost-lock retry loop and signal traps have no test.
why: A deleted retry or trap line leaves every new test green, so the 'holder slower than the stale test' safety is unproven.
fix: Add a test where the owner file changes after acquire (forces the mint-again path), and one that sends TERM mid-wait and asserts the lock folder is gone.
evidence:
holds_lock && break
  held=0   (new lines 169-170); trap 'release_lock; exit 143' TERM (line 155); no test in test_lesson_filing.py touches either

finding: Native-walk test fixture races the 10 s stale takeover.
why: The fresh lock is only removed by the gate's scandir hook; if the gate takes over 10 s, an append takes the lock as stale first and the marker assert fails for a timing reason, not a defect.
fix: Back-date nothing, but make the fixture independent: have the hook, not elapsed time, be the only remover (for example set the lock mtime to now+1 h, or assert after retrying the gate).
evidence: lock.mkdir(parents=True) ... appends = [opened(...)]; ... done = subprocess.run([... GATE ...], timeout=300); assert marker.exists(), output

finding: The 30 s give-up test is a real 30 s sleep with a wall-clock window.
why: It adds about 30 s to every run and the 28 to 60 s window can fail on a loaded machine.
fix: Let the script read an env override for the wait limit so the test waits about 1 s.

finding: Event ts is now stamped before the lock wait, so it can trail ledger order by up to 30 s.
why: Before this change ts was taken immediately before the append; now build_line runs first and the lock wait follows, so a later line can carry an earlier ts (no reader sorts by ts today).
fix: Accept and note it in LEDGER-FORMAT.md, or stamp ts after the lock is held (fill it in with the id).
evidence: line=$(build_line) || bail ...  # then start=$SECONDS; while :; do acquire_lock ...
